notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 2 continuous 50-ft bays, W33X291 girders, one 20-ton pendant crane, bearing on the steps of the existing stepped columns (lower W33X201, upper W14X159) over the lower shafts' crane-side flanges, with top-flange ties to the upper shafts, the rail, bearings and end stops; the stepped columns are checked as two-shaft columns with their existing load effects (effective lengths from a buckling analysis), with the step's local checks, and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.438 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The unstiffened lower web fails J10.2/J10.3 under the upper shaft's inner flange (Lower web · local yielding under the upper inner flange (J10.2)): a stiffener pair under the inner flange (J10.8), the thinnest plate passing the stiffener checks. At the step the tie runs only to the upper shaft's inner face (10.35 in from the girder web), where the sized paired flat bars exceeds its sizing ratio tie-move-root-fatigue (3.87 > 1.00): the existing column is not resized; the checks report the tie. New-steel remedies: a longer tie to a new stub or stand-off on the upper shaft, a column-end slide, or a different tie type.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): H1 top-flange interaction with the load-height LTB strength ratio 0.84, vertical deflection 0.52 and lateral 0.71 of their limits; flanges at least 11.25 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 76 by sizing ratio, 75 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X286: tips ratio 1.18 > 0.85; lateral deflection 1.37 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
